what_happened: The throughput review reported a 'landing and rebuild' stage figure of 1537, then 1842, then 1997 minutes per landed job. It filed high-priority landing-design requests from that figure. The design notes, two verifiers and a redone design all found the figure mostly reflects stacked landing commits, not real waiting. Three design jobs were written on that false premise, and two were rejected for it. The person running Athena did not fix it by hand. They reported it so Athena's loop would fix the measure.
cause: The review treats a computed stage figure as ground truth. Nothing checks it against landing records, earlier verifier findings or design notes that already say the figure is an artifact. Rejected design jobs also send nothing back to the review, so it re-proposes the same work with a worse number each cycle. The stage measure is also not defined to handle stacked commits, so it grows with batching instead of with waiting.
prevention: Two changes together. First, the stage measure should attribute time per job, with stacked landing commits not counted more than once, and the review should check each stage figure against a known-load or per-job sample before it proposes work. Second, the review should read earlier rejected or verifier findings that cite the same figure, and refuse to file a new request from it until those are resolved. This would have stopped all three design jobs.
proposed_request: Fix the throughput review's 'landing and rebuild' stage measure so it reports real waiting time per landed job. Today it reports 1537, then 1842, then 1997 minutes, and the design notes, two verifiers and the redone design say this is mostly a measurement effect of stacked landing commits. Outcome: the measure no longer counts stacked landing commits more than once, and on the existing records it gives a figure consistent with the landing records. Also, before the review proposes work from any stage figure, it checks the figure against earlier rejected jobs and verifier findings that dispute it, and holds the proposal with the reason stated if any exist. Acceptance: run on the recent real landing history, the corrected stage figure is shown next to the old one, with a test that reproduces the stacked-commit inflation. A test shows the review files no landing-design request while a disputing finding is on record. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
